https.title: HTTPS
https.description: TierPlan always serves HTTPS. See the certificate it is using, or get a free one from Let's Encrypt that browsers trust.

note.self_signed: TierPlan made this certificate for this install. Browsers warn about it until you use Let's Encrypt or your own certificate files.
note.cert_files: TierPlan serves the files named by TIERPLAN_TLS_CERT_FILE and TIERPLAN_TLS_KEY_FILE.

acme.title: Let's Encrypt
acme.description: Get a free certificate that browsers trust. TierPlan orders it, renews it by itself and switches to it without a restart. Nobody is signed out.
acme.portNote: Let's Encrypt checks your domain over plain HTTP on port 80. Port 80 on {{host}} must reach TierPlan, for example by starting the container with {{flag}}. TierPlan answers the check on its usual port, so there is nothing else to run.

names.title: Names on the certificate
names.helper: The host of the public URL, plus the host of the agent URL when it is different. Change them in {{link}}. IP addresses and wildcards can't be used.
names.none: No public URL is set yet. Set it in {{link}}.

account.title: Account
account.empty: Let's Encrypt needs an account for this install. TierPlan keeps its key encrypted and never shows it.

email.label: Contact email (optional)
email.helper: Let's Encrypt uses it to reach you about problems with the account. You can leave it empty.
email.error: Enter a valid email address, or leave it empty.

terms.label: I agree to the Let's Encrypt {{link}}
terms.error: Accept the Subscriber Agreement to register.

account.keyNote: TierPlan keeps the account key encrypted and never shows it.

rate_limited.headline: Let's Encrypt is limiting requests.
rate_limited.fix: TierPlan waits until {{time}} before it tries again. There is nothing to do.
rate_limited.fixNoTime: TierPlan waits before it tries again. There is nothing to do.

validation_unreachable.headline: Let's Encrypt couldn't reach http://{{host}}/.well-known/acme-challenge/.
validation_unreachable.fix: Port 80 on {{host}} must reach TierPlan, for example with -p 80:{{port}}. Check your firewall and router, then try again.

validation_dns.headline: The DNS records for {{host}} don't point at this host.
validation_dns.fix: Make the A and AAAA records for {{host}} point at this host. Remove an old AAAA record if you have no IPv6. Then try again.

caa_forbids.headline: A CAA record forbids Let's Encrypt for {{host}}.
caa_forbids.fix: Add a CAA record that allows letsencrypt.org, or remove the one that blocks it.

identifier_rejected.headline: Let's Encrypt won't issue for {{host}}.
identifier_rejected.fix: Use a public DNS name under a domain you own as the public URL.

contact_invalid.headline: Let's Encrypt rejected the contact email.
contact_invalid.fix: Register again with a valid address, or leave it empty.

tos_action_required.headline: Let's Encrypt changed its terms.
tos_action_required.fix: Read the current terms at {{url}}, then try again.

account_gone.headline: Let's Encrypt doesn't know this account.
account_gone.fix: Register the account again in the Account section.

profile_invalid.headline: Let's Encrypt doesn't offer the profile {{profile}}.
profile_invalid.fix: Choose another profile under Advanced, or go back to the CA default.

ca_unavailable.headline: Let's Encrypt couldn't be reached.
ca_unavailable.fix: TierPlan tries again on its own schedule, next at {{time}}. If it keeps failing, check this host's internet access.
ca_unavailable.fixNoTime: TierPlan tries again on its own schedule. If it keeps failing, check this host's internet access.

ca_untrusted.headline: TierPlan doesn't trust the certificate authority's certificate.
ca_untrusted.fix: This only happens with a test directory. Check TIERPLAN_ACME_CA_FILE.

internal.headline: Something went wrong inside TierPlan.
internal.fix: Open Details and check the server log. TierPlan tries again at {{time}}.
internal.fixNoTime: Open Details and check the server log.
